display.purpose: The site masthead only. One per page.

headline.purpose: Georgia section headings, modal titles, empty- and error-state headings. Never inside a card.

date.purpose: The date display. Sans rather than serif because it reads as state, not heading.

title.purpose: Event titles. Never more than ~1.3x body size.

body.purpose: Event descriptions and interface prose, ~70ch inside the 660px column.

document-title.purpose: The h1 on a standalone document page such as Terms. The only h1 that isn't the masthead.

subhead.purpose: Georgia at 1.375rem. Marks an overlay as a distinct place.

section.purpose: Smallest serif step. The 'What's next' heading.

control.purpose: Form fields and button labels. The largest interactive text in the system, deliberately.

control-compact.purpose: Chrome that surrounds content: filter chips, date-nav buttons, footer links, upcoming dates.

meta.purpose: Card apparatus rather than content: location, source link, Share, toggles, counters.

label.purpose: Category tags. Uppercase tracked mono, reads as stamped onto the notice.

time.purpose: The time pill at 0.9375rem. Reads as a peer of the title, not an annotation.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Cards at rest. Barely present by design; lifts paper off the table and nothing more.

shadows.name: hover
shadows.purpose: Card hover, paired with translateY(-2px). The lift is the feedback.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modals only. The one place real two-layer depth is warranted.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Input focus. Soft meadow tint, not a glow.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default control state transitions (buttons, chips, nav).

motion.name: card-stagger
motion.purpose: Per-card entrance delay, hard-capped at 440ms so long days never feel slow.

motion.name: deep-link-pulse
motion.purpose: Twice-pulsing 8px accent ring on a deep-linked card.

components.name: Event Card
components.description: A pinned notice. Hairline border defines it; the resting shadow is near-invisible. Lifts 2px on hover.

components.name: Time Pill
components.description: Signature component. Linen stamp carrying the event time in weathered-leather mono. Shares a 28px min-height with the status badge so the card slot keeps one silhouette.

components.name: Category Tag
components.description: Uppercase mono stamp in its category's colour pair. All six read as one aged family.
components.html: FreeFor kidsMusicSportMarketsTheatre

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Scrolling category filter. Hover previews the category; active inverts to a full category fill.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single accent fill on the page. Hovers toward deep forest ink, not a lighter green.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Transparent with a hairline. Border and text both take the accent on hover; never fills.

components.name: Date Nav Button
components.description: 44px minimum target. The Today variant is the only tinted control on the row.
components.html: <nav class="ds-date-nav"><button class="ds-date-btn">← Previous</button><button class="ds-date-btn ds-date-btn-today">Today</button><button class="ds-date-btn">Pick a date</button><button class="ds-date-btn">Next →</button></nav>

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Hairline field with a visible label above. Focus shifts the border to accent and adds a 3px meadow halo.

components.name: Share Button
components.description: Compact card-footer action. 1.5px border marks it as pressable in a system with almost no fills.

components.name: Modal
components.description: The only surface with real two-layer depth. Linen header with a Georgia title, 16px radius, 540px cap; becomes a bottom sheet below 480px. The scrim is page green, never black.

narrative.overview:
This is the civic board everyone in town reads, given a tasteful upgrade. Each event is a pinned notice: a bordered rectangle of equal weight to every other, carrying its own information and asking for nothing. No notice is promoted, enlarged, or given a photograph to make it shout over its neighbours. The board's job is to hold them all legibly, and the design's job is to disappear into that.

The mood is calm, warm, dependable - unhurried and trustworthy, a page that isn't competing for attention and doesn't need to. Warmth comes from the substrate, not from decoration: an off-white with a green cast (#FAFBF6) rather than clinical white, linen (#F5F0E8) behind the small monospaced details, and a deep forest green that reads as hedgerow rather than corporate. Everything sits on a single 660px column that behaves like a reading measure, not an app viewport. There is no dark mode, no hero, no imagery, and no illustration; the visitor came for an answer and the page gives it in one glance.

The system's discipline is restraint enforced by borders. Surfaces are separated by a 1px hairline (#e0e0d8), not by shadow, colour-blocking, or spacing tricks. The accent green appears on roughly one element per screen. The six category colours have been deliberately weathered into a single earthy family so that no category out-shouts another. The result is a page that looks maintained rather than designed - which, for a community resource run by one person, is exactly the right impression.
keyCharacteristics: Single 660px column, always one card wide, at every breakpoint
Hairline borders define every surface; shadows are near-subliminal
Georgia mastheads over a system sans body; DM Mono reserved strictly for times and tags
Six category colours muted into one aged, sun-faded family
44px minimum touch targets throughout, for an audience that skews older
Light mode only, warm naturals, no imagery whatsoever

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Hedgerow green is the only fully saturated voice on the page and appears as a fill at most once per viewport - the submit button, or the active Today chip, not both competing. Everywhere else it is a text or border colour. Its rarity is what makes the submit action findable without a single arrow or animation.

rules.name: The Aged Family Rule
rules.body: All six category colours must read as the same weathered, sun-faded palette. No category may be brighter, more saturated, or louder than its siblings. Harmony outranks distinguishability here: these are labels on a noticeboard, not a wayfinding system. When adding a category, desaturate it until it sits inside the family, then check it still clears 4.5:1 on its own tint.

rules.name: The Warm Text Rule
rules.body: Text never uses a neutral grey. Every ink carries either the page's green or the palette's brown. #666 and its relatives are banned outright; they are the single fastest way to make this page look like a template.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text colour clears WCAG AA (4.5:1) against every background it is placed on. The audience skews older and this is a product constraint, not a preference. The palette currently has no violations: the tightest pair is Weathered Leather on Linen (the time pill, 13px) at 5.29:1, and every other text pair sits between 5.96:1 and 12.6:1. Weathered Leather was deepened from #8B7355 (3.95:1, failing) to reach this floor.

rules.name: The Serif-Is-Structure Rule
rules.body: Georgia marks a boundary - the masthead, a section heading, a modal title. It never appears inside a card. If serif starts showing up in event content, the hierarchy has collapsed.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Time Rule
rules.body: DM Mono is reserved for times, dates, and the tag stamps. It is never used for body copy, buttons, or emphasis. One webfont, one job.

rules.name: The Modest Title Rule
rules.body: An event title is never more than ~1.3x body size. On a noticeboard every notice is the same size; the day's most interesting event earns attention from its own words, not from typography.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a multi-column event grid at any breakpoint. The single column is the noticeboard; a grid is an aggregator, which is the anti-reference.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Any shadow beyond the resting hairline means the user is doing something - hovering, focusing, or looking at an overlay. Static emphasis must be achieved with type, border, or the accent colour, never with elevation.

rules.name: The Radius-Follows-Scale Rule
rules.body: Never give a small control a large radius or a card a small one. 6 / 8 / 12 / 16 maps to control / button / card / modal, and the ladder is what makes the surfaces feel like one family.

narrative.scope: This system describes the public site (src/). It does not describe public/admin.html, which is an internal operator tool running its own visual language deliberately (Inter and Libre Baskerville, an orange accent, its own radius steps). The owner has confirmed this divergence is intentional and does not want it reconciled. The design-system-* rules and overused-font are switched off for that file alone; contrast, clipping and broken-image checks still apply there.
dos: Do define every surface with the 1px hairline (--border). It is the system's structural element, and removing it in favour of shadow or spacing breaks the noticeboard.
Do keep the events list one column wide at every breakpoint.
Do tint shadows with rgba(26,42,26,...), never pure black - the modal overlay, which falls on the scrim rather than the page, is the sole documented exception.
Do reserve DM Mono for times, dates, and tag stamps.
Do give every interactive control a 44px minimum touch dimension and a real text label - an unlabelled glyph is never the only affordance.
Do put a status badge (ALL DAY, TBC, or a date range) in the card's top-right whenever there is no time, so every card has the same silhouette.
Do desaturate any new category colour into the aged family, then verify it clears 4.5:1 on its own tint.
Do hover primary buttons toward deep forest ink (--ink), not toward a lighter green.
Do extend prefers-reduced-motion coverage explicitly whenever a new transition is added.
donts: Don't use pure #FFFFFF as a page background or neutral grey (#666, #888) for any text. Every neutral in this system carries green or brown.
Don't add a second accent colour. Hedgerow green is the only brand voice, and it appears as a fill roughly once per viewport.
Don't use elevation to signal importance. Shadows respond to interaction; they never rank content.
Don't use a category colour as a background fill anywhere except an active filter chip.
Don't make an event title more than ~1.3x body size, or promote any single event with size, colour, or imagery. Every notice is equal.
Don't introduce photography, illustration, or decorative imagery. The system deliberately has none.
Don't add a dark mode. Light-only with warm naturals is a committed decision, not an oversight.
Don't add an icon library. Text glyphs and inline data-URI SVGs only - the three-dependency budget is a project value.
Don't put the submit call-to-action above the day's events.
Don't use a pill radius (999px) on anything that isn't a time pill or a category tag.
Don't add a webfont beyond DM Mono. Georgia and the system stack are already on the device, and that is the point.
